The '''2024–25 Toronto Maple Leafs season''' was the franchise's 108th season (107th season of play) in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Marion |first1=Laurie |title=2024-25 Toronto Maple Leafs Schedule; Printable, PDF Format - Sports Brackets |url=https://sportsbrackets.net/2024/08/12/2024-25-toronto-maple-leafs-lightning-schedule-printable-pdf-format/ |website=Sports Brackets |publisher=NHL |access-date=October 10, 2024 |date=August 12, 2024}}</ref>

[[Craig Berube]] was hired as head coach of the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]] on May 17, 2024, replacing [[Sheldon Keefe]] after their first-round exit in the [[2024 Stanley Cup playoffs]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/toronto-maple-leafs-hire-craig-berube-as-coach |title=Berube hired as Maple Leafs coach, replaces Keefe |website=NHL.com |date=May 17, 2024 |access-date=May 17, 2024}}</ref>

On April 2, the [[ECHL]] announced that they had terminated the membership of Toronto's affiliate, the [[Newfoundland Growlers]]. The Growlers were experiencing financial difficulties and failure to fulfill financial obligations under ECHL rules.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ECHL's Newfoundland Growlers terminated by league |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/echls-newfoundland-growlers-terminated-by-league/ |access-date=July 25, 2024 |website=Sportsnet.ca}}</ref> The Maple Leafs announced on July 3, that the [[Cincinnati Cyclones]] would be their new ECHL affiliate.<ref>{{Cite web |agency=The Canadian Press |date=July 3, 2024 |title=NHL's Toronto Maple Leafs affiliate with ECHL's Cincinnati Cyclones |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/nhl-s-toronto-maple-leafs-affiliate-with-echl-s-cincinnati-cyclones-1.2144024 |access-date=July 25, 2024 |website=TSN}}</ref>

On August 14, [[Auston Matthews]] was named the 26th captain in Maple Leafs history replacing [[John Tavares]] who held the position since the [[2019–20 Toronto Maple Leafs season|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/mapleleafs/news/maple-leafs-name-auston-matthews-26th-captain-in-franchise-history |title=Maple Leafs Name Auston Matthews 26th Captain in Franchise History |website=NHL.com |date=August 14, 2024 |access-date=August 17, 2024}}</ref>

On April 2, 2025, the Maple Leafs clinched a playoff berth for the ninth consecutive season, after a win over the [[2024–25 Florida Panthers season|Florida Panthers]]. They held the longest active playoff appearance streak at the time, making the playoffs every year since [[2017 Stanley Cup playoffs|2017]] after the [[Boston Bruins]] (previously tied with them for the streak) failed to qualify for the [[2025 Stanley Cup playoffs|2025 playoffs]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/florida-panthers-toronto-maple-leafs-game-recap-april-2 |title=Maple Leafs clinch berth in Stanley Cup Playoffs with win against Panthers. |website=NHL.com |access-date=April 3, 2025 |date=April 2, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/why-boston-bruins-are-eliminated-from-2024-2025-postseason-race |title=Bruins miss playoffs for 1st time since 2015-16 season |website=NHL.com |access-date=April 6, 2025 |date=April 6, 2025}}</ref> Later, on April 15, the Maple Leafs clinched the Atlantic Division championship with a 4–0 win over the [[2024–25 Buffalo Sabres season|Buffalo Sabres]]. This marked the first time that the team won the Atlantic Division since the league realigned prior to the [[2013–14 NHL season|2013–14 season]], their first division championship since winning the temporary [[North Division (NHL)|North Division]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in North America|COVID-19 pandemic]] shortened [[2020–21 Toronto Maple Leafs season|2020–21 season]], and their first standard 82-game regular season division championship since the [[1999–2000 Toronto Maple Leafs season|1999–2000 season]]. This season also saw the Leafs record only four overtime losses, which is the fewest total since [[2003–04 Toronto Maple Leafs season|2003–04]] and the lowest in the salary cap era.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/toronto-maple-leafs-buffalo-sabres-game-recap-april-15 |title=Maple Leafs clinch Atlantic Division with shutout win against Sabres. |website=NHL.com |access-date=April 15, 2025 |date=April 15, 2025}}</ref>

In the first round of the playoffs, the Maple Leafs played the [[2024–25 Ottawa Senators season|Ottawa Senators]] for the first time since the [[2004 Stanley Cup playoffs|2004 playoffs]], reviving the fierce [[Battle of Ontario]] rivalry fought over four series in the early 2000s. Toronto won all four series; however, Ottawa won all three of its games and swept the season series against Toronto this regular season. The Maple Leafs defeated the Senators in six games, advancing to the second round where they lost to the eventual [[Stanley Cup]] champion [[2024–25 Florida Panthers season|Florida Panthers]] in seven games, marking the seventh consecutive game seven loss for the Maple Leafs. This extended the team's [[List of NHL franchise post-season droughts|record-breaking Stanley Cup drought]] to 57 seasons (58 years).

In the process, the Maple Leafs lost a playoff series to an eventual Stanley Cup champion for the first time since [[2000 Stanley Cup playoffs|2000]] when they lost to the [[1999–2000 New Jersey Devils season|New Jersey Devils]]. Their streak of 23 seasons (not counting the [[2004–05 NHL lockout|2004–05 lockout]]) without losing to an eventual champion was the longest in NHL history.{{citation needed|date=May 2026}}

====Notes====
*Toronto will receive the earliest of two picks that San Jose owns.
*Philadelphia will a receive a first-round pick in 2027 if Toronto's first is outside of the top ten selections. 
*Boston will receive a first-round pick in 2026 if Toronto's first is outside of the top five selections and is not conveyed to Chicago.
